transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Sofia Chen (Redwood SE), Andre Valdez (Redwood CSM), Mike Reynolds (Hightide - Procurement), Laura Kim (Hightide - Legal), Priya Patel (Hightide - Head of Platform), Tom Alvarez (Hightide - Security)

Summary:
Kickoff for vendor onboarding and sourcing process. Customer wants clarity on MSA/DPA language, SLA for latency/uptime, pricing paths for hosted vs dedicated, and data residency/KMS requirements for EU and US customers. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC) options. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Contract path: timeline for MSA/DPA redlines and procurement approval
- SLA and SLOs: latency targets, uptime, credits, incident process
- Pricing: committed capacity vs metered hosted; discount triggers and overage billing
- Security: SOC2, encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency
- Technical scope: private deployment network egress, KV cache, quantization and latency testing

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan Meyers from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. We'll run through procurement path, legal asks, and then Sofia will jump into the technical sizing options.
[00:22] Mike: Thanks Jordan. We have Procurement + Legal + Platform on — Laura, Tom, Priya — just to be clear our timeline is tight: we want vendor selection by end of July and a pilot in August.
[00:40] Jordan: Got it. Quick confirm: are you evaluating hosted only or thinking dedicated / on-prem as well?
[00:51] Priya: Both. For payments data we want dedicated or private VPC. For customer-facing chat features we might use hosted for non-PII. So pricing and the data residency part is the blocker.
[01:10] Laura: Legal question up front: do you have a standard DPA we can redline? Also need to see encryption/KMS clauses and subprocessor list.
[01:25] Jordan: Yes we'll send MSA + DPA PDFs that are redline-friendly, and a subprocessor list. We'll flag KMS options — hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default, but Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[01:44] Sofia: And technically that means in private mode we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and disk encryption. There was a recent note about HSM support for FIPS in our private deployment.
[02:05] Tom: Important — Hightide requires HSM-backed keys for payment-related tokens. We need SLA on key lifecycle ops and evidence for attestation.
[02:18] Andre: We'll loop in our security team for the SOC2 artifact pack; can you list the certificates you need and we'll prepare a session?
[02:30] Tom: Yes, a SOC2 evidence call would help. Also want to confirm audit log retention windows — legal may ask for 7 years for some things.
[02:45] Laura: Seven years is long; we may negotiate data retention in DPA for different data classes.
[03:01] Jordan: Noted. Let's talk SLA: we publish latency p95 and availability per routing tier. For hosted our SLA is 99.9% with credits, Dedicated options can reach 99.95 with reserved capacity. We can provide per-route latency SLOs in the contract attachment.
[03:25] Priya: Can you give a rough latency number for the models? If we run 8k context generation p95 what should we expect?
[03:35] Sofia: Rough ballpark depends on model size and batch strategies. For a 13B open model on dedicated A100-type nodes we see ~120–250ms p95 for a short few-hundred-token response. With longer sequences and KV hit rates it increases. We have quantized variants that reduce GPU memory and improve throughput but add a small latency delta.
[04:02] Priya: Ok that's helpful. For our payments flows we need predictable p95 under load spikes. How do you handle graceful degradation?
[04:12] Jordan: We have routing policies: failover to smaller models, autoscale with burst capacity, and can configure conservative CPU-based fallbacks for critical flows. We'll include fallback policies in the rollout section of the MSA.
[04:35] Mike: Pricing — we need committed pricing models and an overage mechanism. Procurement wants a committed capacity discount if we commit to X tokens/month.
[04:48] Jordan: Absolutely. Our pricing sheet includes tiers: hosted metered rates per token, and dedicated reserved pricing with monthly commit and lower unit cost. We also support burst credits and a blended pricing for mixed-mode usage. I'll attach the pricing worksheet after this call.
[05:10] Laura: On billing: do you require a master subscription or can each BU be billed separately? We need to map to procurement org structure.
[05:22] Jordan: We support both: single enterprise invoicing with per-route tagging for chargeback, or multiple billing entities under enterprise accounts. We'll document this in the commercial terms.
[05:35] Priya: Network egress — for private deployment do we have to host any egress endpoints? How is model downloading managed on-prem?
[05:46] Sofia: For on-prem we ship a runtime image; model weights can be pulled from our customer artifact store or delivered via secure transfer. Egress rules depend on your firewall — we can operate air-gapped if needed but that adds extra steps.
[06:05] Tom: For EU data residency, we need data to stay in EU regions and keys managed by EU KMS. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning for both compute and storage?
[06:18] Jordan: Yes, region pinning is available for both hosted and dedicated in supported regions. For private deployments you control the region. We'll include data residency commitments in the DPA.
[06:32] Mike: Procurement checklist: MSA review, DPA review, SSO integration, pricing approval, security attestations. We need to track decision owners.
[06:44] Andre: Perfect — we'll send a checklist doc along with the redlines so it's clear who signs.
[06:52] Laura: A question on indemnity and liability caps — we'll need Redwood's standard positions. Any carveouts for model hallucinations?
[07:04] Jordan: We have standard liability caps tied to fees; hallucination is typically handled as a separate clause — we can propose language that limits liability for model outputs but offers remediation support. We'll propose initial language and mark negotiation points.
[07:26] Priya: For the pilot, can we run a performance benchmark using our prompt sets? We want real-world token distributions not synthetic.
[07:36] Sofia: Yes, we do workload-aware benchmarks. If you share a representative prompt set (obfuscated for PII), we can run a 48–72 hour benchmark on hosted and dedicated sims and give throughput/latency/cost numbers.
[07:53] Priya: We'll need the NDA for sharing that dataset; is a mutual NDA required?
[08:02] Jordan: The MSA includes standard confidentiality. If you need an additional short NDA, Andre can send a one-page mutual NDA.
[08:12] Mike: Timeline recap: decision end of July, pilot start early August. Can we get a draft MSA + DPA and pricing by Friday?
[08:22] Jordan: Yes we'll target 7/10 for docs.
[08:30] Laura: A process note: for commercial approval we route to procurement then legal, and final signed by CFO. If there are non-standard data residency clauses we'll need an exec waiver.
[08:44] Mike: Also add that security needs to see network diagrams and KMS attestation before procurement signs off.
[08:52] Tom: Specifically, we need KMS key handling, HSM attestation, and proof of encryption in transit and at rest. Also integration points for SSO and audit logs.
[09:06] Sofia: We'll prepare diagrams showing where keys live in each deployment model and where audit logs are stored; we can also demonstrate log forwarding to your SIEM via secure syslog or cloud ingestion.
[09:22] Jordan: Competitor question — are you evaluating any other vendors?
[09:26] Mike: We're looking at Anthropic and a couple of managed services from mega cloud providers, and an internal infra path if vendor terms don't meet the residency requirements.
[09:36] Jordan: Noted — we can highlight our private deployment and KMS/HSM story in the redlines doc.
[09:46] Laura: On subcontractors: please include a full subprocessor list. We need to know which third parties touch logs and keys.
[09:55] Jordan: We'll include the subprocessor list and a flow diagram.
[10:05] Priya: A technical detail — how is KV cache persisted in dedicated vs hosted? If we warm caches for low latency, where is that stored and how is it purged?
[10:16] Sofia: KV cache can be in-memory on the serving node for low-latency hits; for persistent caches we use encrypted object stores; purge policies are configurable and we can expose APIs to purge per-customer keys. We'll document purge semantics in the operations appendix.
[10:33] Priya: Good. Also need an SLO on cache warm-up times for the pilot.
[10:41] Sofia: We'll include expected warm-up curves given your prompt distributions from the benchmark.
[10:50] Mike: Can you summarize the negotiated SLAs and what counts as an outage?
[10:56] Jordan: Outage is defined as service unavailability preventing API responses; latency degradations below thresholds are SLA breaches for certain plans. Credits are pro-rated based on downtime window; specifics in the SLA exhibit. For Dedicated we can add tighter SLOs with financial credits.
[11:15] Laura: On export controls and data jurisdiction, if we process EU personal data from customers in the EU, who is the data controller/processor?
[11:27] Jordan: Hightide will be the controller, Redwood the processor. We'll list processing roles in the DPA and include subprocessors and transfers clauses.
[11:40] Tom: What about encryption key escrow? We need to ensure Redwood can't unilaterally access keys in customer-managed KMS.
[11:51] Sofia: With customer-managed KMS, keys are under your control — we don't have plaintext access. For managed keys we offer strict access controls and audited key usage.
[12:04] Mike: Let's talk redlines: Laura will propose changes to indemnity and data retention. Will Redwood accept limited liability and carveouts?
[12:16] Jordan: We'll review but expect negotiation. We'll mark essential clauses that are not negotiable and provide rationale for those.
[12:28] Laura: Last question for now — do you have a pricing accelerator for committed multi-year deals?
[12:35] Jordan: Yes, committed multi-year or capacity commitments get stepped discounts and operational credits. We'll put examples in the pricing workbook.
[12:48] Priya: For the pilot, can we get a sandbox that mirrors production routing so we can test fallbacks?
[12:56] Sofia: Yes we can provide a pilot tenant with production-like routing. There may be small differences but we'll try to mirror SLOs.
[13:10] Andre: To recap next steps: Jordan uploads MSA/DPA/pricing; Sofia schedules the private-deploy sketch and benchmarking; Tom and Andre schedule SOC2 evidence call; Laura sends procurement timeline.
[13:28] Mike: Sounds good. Anything else?
[13:33] Laura: We'll look at the MSA and return initial redlines; if there are major exceptions we expect a short negotiation cycle.
[13:42] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the checklist and docs.
